method: Read under subscription in the operator's browser and PARAPHRASED. No AMH passage reproduced and no source_text stored; every claim carries a locator and verdict licensed_source_not_quoted. Dose claims flagged dose:true. The ten injectable cytokine modulators are named but none of their monographs was retrieved and no biological dose appears here. Ciclosporin carries no psoriasis-specific dose in AMH (seek specialist advice) and none is reconstructed. The apremilast renal dose reduction was truncated in retrieval and the reduced dose is NOT stated. Folate co-prescription with methotrexate was not covered in the retrieved sections and was not imported from elsewhere. eTG CROSS-CHECK 2026-09-24: every licensed-source dose compared with Therapeutic Guidelines (paraphrased, no eTG text stored); results and additions in the page's eTG cross-check section.

claims.claim: Plaque psoriasis is the most common form of this chronic inflammatory disease and classically affects elbows, knees, buttocks and scalp
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Choice of treatment depends on disease severity and location, comorbidities including psoriatic arthritis, and response to previous therapy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients should be referred to a dermatologist if appropriate topical therapy fails, if phototherapy or systemic treatment is needed, or if psoriasis is pustular, severe or extensive
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Potential triggers to minimise or eliminate include stress, trauma, smoking, alcohol, infections, and drugs such as lithium, hydroxychloroquine, ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Streptococcal throat infection may precipitate guttate psoriasis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients with psoriasis have increased cardiovascular risk and possibly metabolic syndrome compared with the general population, so cardiovascular risk factors should be managed and smoking discouraged
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Before immunosuppressants or cytokine modulators, consider present or latent infection such as hepatitis B and TB, immunisation requirements especially live vaccines, and history of malignant disease
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Pneumococcal and annual influenza vaccination should be considered for patients taking immunosuppressants or cytokine modulators
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Patients should be monitored for development of psoriatic arthritis with rheumatology consultation considered if suspected
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical treatment is used for most patients with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis and as an adjunct to phototherapy or systemic treatment in more severe disease, with agents commonly combined
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Moisturisers hydrate skin, soften scaling and reduce itching and irritation, are encouraged particularly after bathing, and emollient soap substitutes or fragrance-free bath oils are advised
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Topical corticosteroids are a first-line option, chosen by potency and formulation according to severity, location, patient preference and age, with mild corticosteroids useful on face, flexures and genitals
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Psoriasis symptoms can worsen quickly after stopping topical corticosteroids, particularly when treatment is stopped abruptly
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Calcipotriol has similar efficacy to potent or very potent corticosteroids, is only available combined with betamethasone which is more effective than either agent alone, and can irritate particularly the face or flexures
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Salicylic acid is a keratolytic that reduces scaling and softens plaques and is often used with coal tar, dithranol and corticosteroids to help them penetrate lesions and increase efficacy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Coal tar is particularly used for scalp, hands and feet and can be used for guttate psoriasis, but preparations are messy, stain clothing, smell unpleasant, are photosensitising and may be irritant
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Dithranol is rarely used because it is irritant and stains clothing, skin and hair, and should be avoided on the face, flexures and genitals
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Phototherapy uses UV light to reduce skin inflammation and includes narrow-band or broad-band UVB and photochemotherapy with topical or oral methoxsalen plus UVA, generally given 2 or 3 times per week for a few months with repeat courses sometimes needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Systemic treatment is used for severe or extensive psoriasis, or for less severe psoriasis when topical therapy or phototherapy is inadequate or inappropriate
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Methotrexate is an immunosuppressant for severe psoriasis requiring careful monitoring particularly for myelosuppression and hepatotoxicity
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Ciclosporin is an immunosuppressant for severe psoriasis requiring careful monitoring particularly for nephrotoxicity and hypertension
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Apremilast is an oral cytokine modulator that may reduce TNF-alpha and interleukins 17 and 23 and increase interleukin 10, used when methotrexate is inadequate or inappropriate
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Acitretin is an oral retinoid for severe psoriasis such as pustular, erythrodermic, palm or sole psoriasis, and is rarely used in women of child-bearing potential because of teratogenicity
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Injectable cytokine modulators are usually used for severe psoriasis when phototherapy, methotrexate, ciclosporin, acitretin or apremilast is inadequate or inappropriate, many also treat psoriatic arthritis, and they can cause immunosuppression and increase infection risk
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Interleukin inhibitors used in psoriasis include guselkumab, ixekizumab, risankizumab, secukinumab, tildrakizumab and ustekinumab, and TNF-alpha antagonists include adalimumab, certolizumab, etanercept and infliximab
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Psoriasis' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for psoriasis), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Calcipotriol with betamethasone has a maximum daily dose of 15 g and maximum weekly dose of 100 g and should not be applied to more than 30 percent of body surface
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Calcipotriol with betamethasone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-psoriasis/other-drugs-psoriasis/calcipotriol-betamethasone, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Calcipotriol with betamethasone cream is applied to affected scalp, trunk and limbs once a day for up to 8 weeks in adults, and the foam once a day for up to 4 weeks
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Calcipotriol with betamethasone' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-psoriasis/other-drugs-psoriasis/calcipotriol-betamethasone, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Methotrexate is taken once a week on the same day each week
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Methotrexate (immunomodulator)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/immunomodulators-anti-inflammatories/other-immunomodulators/methotrexate-immunomodulator, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Methotrexate for adults is oral, subcutaneous or intramuscular, initially 10 to 15 mg once a week adjusted to response, with usual maintenance 10 to 25 mg once a week and maximum oral 30 mg or parenteral 25 mg
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Methotrexate (immunomodulator)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/immunomodulators-anti-inflammatories/other-immunomodulators/methotrexate-immunomodulator, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: When changing methotrexate from oral to subcutaneous or intramuscular, consider reducing the dose and monitoring carefully especially for oral doses above 15 mg because parenteral bioavailability is higher
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Methotrexate (immunomodulator)' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/immunomodulators-anti-inflammatories/other-immunomodulators/methotrexate-immunomodulator, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Ciclosporin dose and duration differ by disease and specialist advice should be sought
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Ciclosporin' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/immunomodulators-anti-inflammatories/calcineurin-inhibitors/ciclosporin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Apremilast is oral, initially 10 mg once on day 1, then 10 mg twice on day 2, increasing by 10 mg each day to 30 mg twice a day, with treatment stopped if there is no response after 24 weeks and dose reduced if CrCl is under 30 mL per minute
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Apremilast' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-psoriasis/immunosuppressants-dermatology/apremilast, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Acitretin in adults is oral 25 to 30 mg once daily for 2 to 4 weeks then maintenance generally 25 to 50 mg once a day based on efficacy and tolerance, and in children 0.5 to 1 mg/kg once daily with a usual maximum of 35 mg daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Acitretin' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-acne/retinoids-oral/acitretin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Trunk/limb chronic plaque psoriasis: LPC (coal tar solution) 4-8% + salicylic acid 3% cream/ointment topically twice daily for 1 month first-line; add methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% or mometasone 0.1% once daily until clear (2-6 weeks), stepping to betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% if inadequate after 3 weeks.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Plaque psoriasis treatment according to location: Trunk and limbs'

claims.claim: Scalp psoriasis: methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% lotion or mometasone 0.1% lotion/hydrogel once daily (2-6 weeks); if inadequate after 2 weeks betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% lotion twice daily or clobetasol 0.05% shampoo daily for 6 weeks; then coal tar shampoo; calcipotriol+betamethasone foam daily if uncontrolled; LPC 4-8% + salicylic acid 3% pomade twice daily for thick scale.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Plaque psoriasis treatment according to location: Scalp'

claims.claim: Face: methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% (centre face) or mometasone 0.1% (ears/hairline) once daily 2-6 weeks; child hydrocortisone 1%; maintenance LPC 2% + salicylic acid 2% at night; avoid calcipotriol on face.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Plaque psoriasis treatment according to location: Face'

claims.claim: Flexural/genital psoriasis: methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% ointment once daily (max 2 weeks under nappies, add anticandidal), then LPC 2% in emulsifying ointment daily (no salicylic acid).
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Flexural psoriasis, including genital psoriasis'

claims.claim: Palmoplantar: hyperkeratotic - LPC 4-8% + salicylic acid 6% twice daily for 1 month or calcipotriol+betamethasone once daily ~6 weeks; pustular - betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% or mometasone 0.1% ointment daily 2-6 weeks, escalate to betamethasone in optimised vehicle. Nails: calcipotriol+betamethasone ointment nightly up to 3 months.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Palms and soles / Nails'

claims.claim: Do not use oral corticosteroids for psoriasis (risk of generalised pustular flare); generalised pustular psoriasis is an emergency requiring hospital referral; offer HIV testing for severe/recalcitrant psoriasis.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Dermatology guideline: 'Psoriasis' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Dermatology&topicfile=c_DMG_Considerations-in-the-use-of-topical-corticosteroids_topic_1&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_DMG_Psoriasis_topic_2, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Advice for managing psoriasis in primary care / Other types of psoriasis'
